exercises.skill: Two modal verbs in one clause (müssen + können)
exercises.english: You must be able to reach me by phone today.
exercises.german: Du musst mich heute noch telefonisch erreichen können.
exercises.why: The finite modal is müssen, the full verb is erreichen and können closes the clause as the second level.

exercises.skill: Two modal verbs in one clause (müssen + können)
exercises.english: I have to be able to work on Sundays every now and then.
exercises.german: Ich muss ab und zu sonntags arbeiten können.
exercises.why: Necessity plus ability, with the time expression ab und zu in the middle field.

exercises.skill: Two modal verbs in one clause (müssen + können)
exercises.english: The apprentice must be able to explain the mistake to the customer.
exercises.german: Die Auszubildende muss den Kunden den Fehler erklären können.
exercises.why: The accusative object den Kunden stands in the field, and the double infinitive closes the clause.

exercises.skill: Two modal verbs in one clause (müssen + können)
exercises.english: You must be able to apologise for the mistake.
exercises.german: Du musst dich für den Fehler entschuldigen können.
exercises.why: The reflexive pronoun sich is accusative and belongs in the field before the closing cluster.

exercises.skill: Two modal verbs in one clause (müssen + können)
exercises.english: We have to be able to book the room online.
exercises.german: Wir müssen das Zimmer online buchen können.
exercises.why: A simple müssen and können stack with the determiner das Zimmer in the field.

exercises.skill: Two modal verbs in one clause (müssen + können)
exercises.english: You must be able to reach your boss even while he is on holiday.
exercises.german: Du musst den Chef auch im Urlaub erreichen können.
exercises.why: Two modal levels with the prepositional phrase auch im Urlaub in the field.

exercises.skill: Two modal verbs in one clause (müssen + können)
exercises.english: A nurse has to be able to recognise a severe reaction.
exercises.german: Eine Pflegekraft muss eine schwere Reaktion erkennen können.
exercises.why: The indefinite article of the subject is kept and the modal stack ends the clause.

exercises.skill: Two modal verbs in one clause (müssen + können)
exercises.english: You must be able to find the file without help.
exercises.german: Du musst die Datei ohne Hilfe finden können.
exercises.why: The bare noun ohne Hilfe is the first level of the obligation, the second is the ability to find it.

exercises.skill: Two modal verbs in one clause (müssen + können)
exercises.english: The teacher must be able to explain the rule in simple words.
exercises.german: Die Lehrerin muss die Regel in einfachen Worten erklären können.
exercises.why: The verb position stays second in the main clause while the two infinitives sit at the end.

exercises.skill: Two modal verbs in one clause (müssen + können)
exercises.english: You must be able to get a receipt at the customer service.
exercises.german: Du musst beim Kundenservice einen Beleg bekommen können.
exercises.why: The second modal können is the infinitive of müssen and closes the sentence after the full verb.

exercises.skill: Two modal verbs in one clause (müssen + können)
exercises.english: He has to be able to say no to his own boss.
exercises.german: Er muss Nein zu seinem Chef sagen können.
exercises.why: The verb sagen with a prepositional object in the field, then können as the second level.

exercises.skill: Two modal verbs in one clause (müssen + können)
exercises.english: You must be able to say that honestly.
exercises.german: Du musst das ehrlich sagen können.
exercises.why: A short two-level clause where the modal infinitive follows the full verb directly.

exercises.skill: Two modal verbs in one clause (müssen + können)
exercises.english: I want to be able to go swimming again after the injury.
exercises.german: Ich will nach der Verletzung wieder ins Schwimmbad gehen können.
exercises.why: Here wollen is the outer level and können the inner one, so the two meanings are will plus ability.

exercises.skill: Two modal verbs in one clause (müssen + können)
exercises.english: I do not want to have to ask my landlord about every single thing.
exercises.german: Ich will nicht für alles meinen Vermieter fragen müssen.
exercises.why: A pure modal stack with only one nicht, placed after the finite modal wollen.

exercises.skill: Two modal verbs in one clause (müssen + können)
exercises.english: We have to be able to manage without a car.
exercises.german: Wir müssen ohne Auto zurechtkommen können.
exercises.why: Idiomatic zurechtkommen takes a können infinitive to express coping on one's own.

exercises.skill: Two modal verbs in one clause (müssen + können)
exercises.english: You must be able to read the meter correctly.
exercises.german: Du musst den Zähler richtig ablesen können.
exercises.why: The separable verb ablesen loses its prefix and appears in the infinitive at the end.

exercises.skill: Two modal verbs in one clause (müssen + können)
exercises.english: The employee must be able to meet the deadline during the holidays as well.
exercises.german: Die Mitarbeiterin muss die Frist auch in den Ferien einhalten können.
exercises.why: The accusative object die Frist stays in the field, and both infinitives close the clause.

exercises.skill: Two modal verbs in one clause (müssen + können)
exercises.english: I have to be able to check the numbers again at home.
exercises.german: Ich muss die Zahlen zu Hause noch einmal kontrollieren können.
exercises.why: A three-part field of place, time and object between the finite modal and the closing cluster.

exercises.skill: Two modal verbs in one clause (müssen + können)
exercises.english: Our guests must be able to get to the fourth floor without a lift.
exercises.german: Die Gäste müssen auch ohne Aufzug in den vierten Stock kommen können.
exercises.why: A modal stack on a prefixed motion verb: kommen können expresses mobility, not permission.

exercises.skill: Two modal verbs in one clause (müssen + können)
exercises.english: He has to be able to take the train to the airport.
exercises.german: Er muss mit dem Zug zum Flughafen fahren können.
exercises.why: The means of transport sits in the field, and fahren können forms the second level.

exercises.skill: Modal verb as the infinitive of another modal
exercises.english: I have to be able to cope with all of that.
exercises.german: Ich muss das alles verkraften können.
exercises.why: The modal können is the infinitive of müssen and stands behind the full verb verkraften.

exercises.skill: Modal verb as the infinitive of another modal
exercises.english: You have to be able to find your way here on your own.
exercises.german: Du musst dich hier ohne Hilfe orientieren können.
exercises.why: The reflexive pronoun is accusative and the modal infinitive closes the two-level bracket.

exercises.skill: Modal verb as the infinitive of another modal
exercises.english: He has to be able to stand the new pace.
exercises.german: Er muss das neue Tempo aushalten können.
exercises.why: A separable prefix verb in the Infinitiv I, with können as the second modal level.

exercises.skill: Modal verb as the infinitive of another modal
exercises.english: She has to be able to cope on her own.
exercises.german: Sie muss von allein zurechtkommen können.
exercises.why: A must-phrase about independence, expressed as a modal plus a modal plus a full verb.

exercises.skill: Modal verb as the infinitive of another modal
exercises.english: You all have to be able to afford that.
exercises.german: Ihr müsst euch das leisten können.
exercises.why: The accusative reflexive pronoun euch belongs in the field, and the second modal is können.

exercises.skill: Modal verb as the infinitive of another modal
exercises.english: People have to be able to deal with a refusal.
exercises.german: Man muss mit einer Ablehnung umgehen können.
exercises.why: Impersonal man takes a können infinitive, giving general necessity plus general capacity.

exercises.skill: Modal verb as the infinitive of another modal
exercises.english: I have to be able to react to it.
exercises.german: Ich muss darauf reagieren können.
exercises.why: A very short stack: modal, field with a prepositional object, full verb, modal infinitive.

exercises.skill: Modal verb as the infinitive of another modal
exercises.english: You have to be able to answer for that.
exercises.german: Du musst das verantworten können.
exercises.why: A two-level clause with no separable prefix and no auxiliary: only the two modals govern the content.

exercises.skill: Modal verb as the infinitive of another modal
exercises.english: He has to be able to bear the consequences.
exercises.german: Er muss die Folgen tragen können.
exercises.why: The full verb tragen is followed by the second modal, which is the compulsory order.

exercises.skill: Modal verb as the infinitive of another modal
exercises.english: We have to be able to come to terms with it.
exercises.german: Wir müssen damit klarkommen können.
exercises.why: The middle field holds a pronoun standing for the situation, and the modal stack closes the clause.

exercises.skill: Modal verb as the infinitive of another modal
exercises.english: You have to be able to register in person.
exercises.german: Du musst dich persönlich anmelden können.
exercises.why: A reflexive full verb plus a können infinitive, both at the end in that order.

exercises.skill: Modal verb as the infinitive of another modal
exercises.english: You all have to be able to arrange that yourselves.
exercises.german: Ihr müsst das bewerkstelligen können.
exercises.why: A modal addressing a group, with the modal infinitive as the second level of the closing element.

exercises.skill: Modal verb as the infinitive of another modal
exercises.english: Pupils have to be able to understand that.
exercises.german: Die Schüler müssen das nachvollziehen können.
exercises.why: Plural subject, single verb in the middle field, and the modal stack at the end.

exercises.skill: Modal verb as the infinitive of another modal
exercises.english: One has to be able to make use of this offer.
exercises.german: Man muss von diesem Angebot Gebrauch machen können.
exercises.why: A fixed prepositional phrase stays in the field while können closes the sentence.

exercises.skill: Modal verb as the infinitive of another modal
exercises.english: You have to be able to work here without help.
exercises.german: Du musst hier ohne Hilfe arbeiten können.
exercises.why: Place and qualifier in the field, arbeiten as the Infinitiv I and können as the Infinitiv II.

exercises.skill: Modal verb as the infinitive of another modal
exercises.english: She has to be able to look after herself.
exercises.german: Sie muss auf sich selbst aufpassen können.
exercises.why: The reflexive pronoun sits in the accusative field, and the modal infinitive completes the stack.

exercises.skill: Modal verb as the infinitive of another modal
exercises.english: He has to be able to get used to it.
exercises.german: Er muss sich auf die neue Lage einstellen können.
exercises.why: A separable verb appears without its prefix in the infinitive, followed by the modal level.

exercises.skill: Modal verb as the infinitive of another modal
exercises.english: Everyone has to be able to enforce their own rights.
exercises.german: Alle müssen ihre Rechte durchsetzen können.
exercises.why: The indefinite pronoun is the subject of the finite modal, and können closes the clause.

exercises.skill: Modal verb as the infinitive of another modal
exercises.english: You have to be able to express your opinion.
exercises.german: Du musst deine Meinung äußern können.
exercises.why: An umlaut verb in the Infinitiv I plus a können infinitive, both at the end.

exercises.skill: Modal verb as the infinitive of another modal
exercises.english: You have to be able to assess the situation.
exercises.german: Du musst die Lage einschätzen können.
exercises.why: A two-level clause whose first modal is a must, not a want, so the obligation stays visible.

exercises.skill: Perfekt of modal verbs as the second level
exercises.english: He has had to come to the office twice this week.
exercises.german: Er hat in dieser Woche zweimal ins Büro kommen müssen.
exercises.why: The Perfekt of a modal: hat plus kommen plus the modal infinitive müssen, with no participle.

exercises.skill: Perfekt of modal verbs as the second level
exercises.english: I have had to cancel the appointment.
exercises.german: Ich habe den Termin absagen müssen.
exercises.why: The double infinitive reports a completed obligation; absagen precedes the modal level.

exercises.skill: Perfekt of modal verbs as the second level
exercises.english: She was allowed to go home early.
exercises.german: Sie hat früher gehen dürfen.
exercises.why: In the Perfekt, permission is expressed with the dürfen infinitive, not with a participle.

exercises.skill: Perfekt of modal verbs as the second level
exercises.english: You have had to warn her.
exercises.german: Du hast sie warnen müssen.
exercises.why: A two-part Perfekt with the full verb first and the modal infinitive as the closer.

exercises.skill: Perfekt of modal verbs as the second level
exercises.english: We had to wait two hours for the visa.
exercises.german: Wir haben zwei Stunden auf das Visum warten müssen.
exercises.why: A duration in the field, a directional verb as Infinitiv I and the obligation as the second level.

exercises.skill: Perfekt of modal verbs as the second level
exercises.english: He has had to postpone the exam.
exercises.german: Er hat die Prüfung verschieben müssen.
exercises.why: A common exam-context Perfekt with the modal infinitive in the final position.

exercises.skill: Perfekt of modal verbs as the second level
exercises.english: I have had to go to the police.
exercises.german: Ich habe zur Polizei gehen müssen.
exercises.why: The modal Perfekt of a directional verb, with the destination in the field.

exercises.skill: Perfekt of modal verbs as the second level
exercises.english: They were not allowed to enter the room.
exercises.german: Sie haben den Raum nicht betreten dürfen.
exercises.why: Negation belongs to the inner level and the modal infinitive dürfen closes the clause.

exercises.skill: Perfekt of modal verbs as the second level
exercises.english: You should have warned me.
exercises.german: Du hättest mich warnen sollen.
exercises.why: Konjunktiv II in the past uses hätte plus Infinitiv I plus modal infinitive to express regret.

exercises.skill: Perfekt of modal verbs as the second level
exercises.english: She has had to work overtime several times.
exercises.german: Sie hat mehrmals Überstunden machen müssen.
exercises.why: The multiword noun Überstunden stays accusative in the field of the double infinitive.

exercises.skill: Perfekt of modal verbs as the second level
exercises.english: He has had to sign for the package.
exercises.german: Er hat für das Paket unterschreiben müssen.
exercises.why: A separable prefix verb appears in the Infinitiv I, followed by the modal infinitive.

exercises.skill: Perfekt of modal verbs as the second level
exercises.english: I have been able to finish the work.
exercises.german: Ich habe die Arbeit fertig machen können.
exercises.why: The second level is the ability, reported retrospectively by the können infinitive.

exercises.skill: Perfekt of modal verbs as the second level
exercises.english: We have been able to pay by card.
exercises.german: Wir haben mit Karte bezahlen können.
exercises.why: A modal Perfekt whose modal infinitive expresses a capacity that has been used up.

exercises.skill: Perfekt of modal verbs as the second level
exercises.english: Did you have to pay extra?
exercises.german: Hast du extra zahlen müssen?
exercises.why: A yes/no question keeps the auxiliary in position two and both infinitives at the end.

exercises.skill: Perfekt of modal verbs as the second level
exercises.english: She has had to learn German from scratch.
exercises.german: Sie hat Deutsch ganz neu lernen müssen.
exercises.why: A whole object phrase stays in the field, and the obligation is the second level.

exercises.skill: Perfekt of modal verbs as the second level
exercises.english: They have been able to stay in the old flat.
exercises.german: Sie haben in der alten Wohnung bleiben können.
exercises.why: Ability as the second level of a modal Perfekt, with the location in the field.

exercises.skill: Perfekt of modal verbs as the second level
exercises.english: He has had to leave the country once more.
exercises.german: Er hat das Land noch einmal verlassen müssen.
exercises.why: A Perfekt with a prefixed full verb, which is inserted between hat and the modal infinitive.

exercises.skill: Perfekt of modal verbs as the second level
exercises.english: You have had to work without a break.
exercises.german: Du hast ohne Pause arbeiten müssen.
exercises.why: The Perfekt auxiliary replaces the present modal, but the modal infinitive still closes the clause.

exercises.skill: Perfekt of modal verbs as the second level
exercises.english: I have not been able to reach you.
exercises.german: Ich habe dich nicht erreichen können.
exercises.why: One nicht after the auxiliary denies the whole perfect clause, including the second level.

exercises.skill: Perfekt of modal verbs as the second level
exercises.english: She has had to look after her sick father.
exercises.german: Sie hat ihren kranken Vater versorgen müssen.
exercises.why: The possessive article and adjective stay in the accusative field of the double infinitive.

exercises.skill: Modal stacks in subordinate clauses
exercises.english: He says that we have to start earlier.
exercises.german: Er sagt, dass wir früher anfangen müssen.
exercises.why: A modal in a dass-clause stands last; the accusative object stays in the field.

exercises.skill: Modal stacks in subordinate clauses
exercises.english: I do not think that he is allowed to do that.
exercises.german: Ich glaube nicht, dass er das machen darf.
exercises.why: A modal subordinate clause: negation sits on the matrix verb, the modal closes the clause.

exercises.skill: Modal stacks in subordinate clauses
exercises.english: It is important that you are not allowed to forget the deadline.
exercises.german: Es ist wichtig, dass du die Frist nicht vergessen darfst.
exercises.why: A dass-clause with a negated modal in the last position and the object in the field.

exercises.skill: Modal stacks in subordinate clauses
exercises.english: She explained that she had to look after the dog.
exercises.german: Sie hat erklärt, dass sie den Hund hat versorgen müssen.
exercises.why: The subordinate Perfekt has its own hat plus double infinitive inside an outer perfect clause.

exercises.skill: Modal stacks in subordinate clauses
exercises.english: Please go to the counter so that you can sign the form.
exercises.german: Gehen Sie bitte zum Schalter, damit Sie das Formular unterschreiben können.
exercises.why: damit is required here, because a modal verb at the end rules out um zu.

exercises.skill: Modal stacks in subordinate clauses
exercises.english: I need to call you so that you can get the pictures printed today.
exercises.german: Ich muss dich heute noch anrufen, damit du die Bilder ausdrucken kannst.
exercises.why: The main clause carries the modal intention, the damit-clause the second level of ability.

exercises.skill: Modal stacks in subordinate clauses
exercises.english: She was annoyed that she was not allowed to speak.
exercises.german: Sie war ärgert, dass sie nicht sprechen durfte.
exercises.why: A past modal in a subordinate clause reports the state of affairs at that moment.

exercises.skill: Modal stacks in subordinate clauses
exercises.english: The rule is that students are not allowed to use their phones.
exercises.german: Die Regel ist, dass die Schüler ihre Handys nicht benutzen dürfen.
exercises.why: The negated modal in the dass-clause expresses the prohibition the rule contains.

exercises.skill: Modal stacks in subordinate clauses
exercises.english: Although he has to work late, he still comes to the course.
exercises.german: Obwohl er spät arbeiten muss, kommt er zum Kurs.
exercises.why: The modal sits at the end of the obwohl-clause, the main clause keeps verb two.

exercises.skill: Modal stacks in subordinate clauses
exercises.english: I need to know whether we are allowed to park here.
exercises.german: Ich muss wissen, ob wir hier parken dürfen.
exercises.why: A matrix modal in the main clause plus a second modal level inside the ob-clause.

exercises.skill: Modal stacks in subordinate clauses
exercises.english: The lawyer asked whether we have to pay the costs.
exercises.german: Der Anwalt hat gefragt, ob wir die Kosten tragen müssen.
exercises.why: An indirect question with the modal at the end and the object in the subordinate field.

exercises.skill: Modal stacks in subordinate clauses
exercises.english: The teacher demanded that we hand in the report by Friday.
exercises.german: Die Lehrerin verlangte, dass wir den Bericht bis Freitag abgeben sollen.
exercises.why: Reported instruction takes sollen, not müssen, because the obligation comes from a third party.

exercises.skill: Modal stacks in subordinate clauses
exercises.english: She apologised for having to cancel the trip.
exercises.german: Sie entschuldigte sich dafür, dass sie die Reise absagen musste.
exercises.why: The modal of obligation stands last in the dass-clause after the preposition dafür.

exercises.skill: Modal stacks in subordinate clauses
exercises.english: Whoever is allowed to park here has to pay at the machine.
exercises.german: Wer hier parken darf, muss am Automaten bezahlen.
exercises.why: The relative clause holds the permission level, the main clause the payment obligation.

exercises.skill: Modal stacks in subordinate clauses
exercises.english: I am pleased that we can start at eight.
exercises.german: Ich freue mich, dass wir um acht anfangen können.
exercises.why: A können subordinate clause after a matrix verb, with the time in the subordinate field.

exercises.skill: Modal stacks in subordinate clauses
exercises.english: You need a visa so that you can enter the country.
exercises.german: Du brauchst ein Visum, um in das Land einreisen zu können.
exercises.why: An um zu-clause is fine as long as its final word is the zu infinitive, not a modal.

exercises.skill: Modal stacks in subordinate clauses
exercises.english: He was annoyed that he had to wait for an hour.
exercises.german: Er ärgerte sich darüber, dass er eine Stunde warten musste.
exercises.why: A dass-clause with a duration in the field and the modal obligation as the closer.

exercises.skill: Modal stacks in subordinate clauses
exercises.english: It makes a difference whether you can come or not.
exercises.german: Es ist egal, ob du kommen kannst oder nicht.
exercises.why: The ob-clause carries a können present form, and oder nicht keeps the negation outside it.

exercises.skill: Modal stacks in subordinate clauses
exercises.english: She said that she would have to move the delivery to Monday.
exercises.german: Sie sagte, dass sie die Lieferung auf Montag verschieben müsste.
exercises.why: Reported obligation in Konjunktiv II, with the verb last in the dass-clause.

exercises.skill: Modal stacks in subordinate clauses
exercises.english: I think it is right that we can still fill in the form online today.
exercises.german: Ich finde es richtig, dass wir das Formular heute noch online ausfüllen können.
exercises.why: A können modal closes the dass-clause while the matrix verb keeps its place in the main clause.

exercises.skill: Choosing the right modal for strength and relationship
exercises.english: I have to leave now.
exercises.german: Ich muss jetzt gehen.
exercises.why: Objective necessity is müssen, and it takes no second modal because no ability is in question.

exercises.skill: Choosing the right modal for strength and relationship
exercises.english: You are not allowed to park here.
exercises.german: Du darfst hier nicht parken.
exercises.why: A prohibition is a negated dürfen, not a negated müssen.

exercises.skill: Choosing the right modal for strength and relationship
exercises.english: Please compare the two contracts.
exercises.german: Die beiden Verträge sollen Sie bitte vergleichen.
exercises.why: Instruction reported by a third party takes sollen, with Sie in the field.

exercises.skill: Choosing the right modal for strength and relationship
exercises.english: I do not feel like going out tonight.
exercises.german: Ich mag heute Abend nicht ausgehen.
exercises.why: Inclination is mögen; a negated mögen is a preference, not a prohibition.

exercises.skill: Choosing the right modal for strength and relationship
exercises.english: I would like to book a table for two.
exercises.german: Ich möchte einen Tisch für zwei reservieren.
exercises.why: möchte is the polite form of wollen and never expresses necessity.

exercises.skill: Choosing the right modal for strength and relationship
exercises.english: I will not sign that.
exercises.german: Ich will das nicht unterschreiben.
exercises.why: A decision of the speaker is wollen, not müssen, so no second level is added.

exercises.skill: Choosing the right modal for strength and relationship
exercises.english: You should see a doctor.
exercises.german: Du solltest einen Arzt aufsuchen.
exercises.why: Advice from the speaker is sollen in Konjunktiv II, weaker than müssen.

exercises.skill: Choosing the right modal for strength and relationship
exercises.english: He has to work night shifts this month.
exercises.german: Er muss diesen Monat Nachtschichten machen.
exercises.why: A fixed external requirement is müssen, with the plural noun as the accusative object.

exercises.skill: Choosing the right modal for strength and relationship
exercises.english: You must not forget the keys.
exercises.german: Du musst die Schlüssel nicht vergessen.
exercises.why: A negated müssen denies the necessity itself here; a rule would take dürfen nicht instead.

exercises.skill: Choosing the right modal for strength and relationship
exercises.english: I have to make the 6:15 train.
exercises.german: Ich muss den Zug um 6:15 Uhr noch erreichen.
exercises.why: A single modal suffices, because only one level of necessity is meant.

exercises.skill: Choosing the right modal for strength and relationship
exercises.english: It would be better if you came with us.
exercises.german: Es wäre besser, wenn du mit uns kommst.
exercises.why: An unreal condition uses Konjunktiv II in the wenn-clause with a single modal at the end.

exercises.skill: Choosing the right modal for strength and relationship
exercises.english: Am I allowed to open the window?
exercises.german: Darf ich das Fenster öffnen?
exercises.why: A yes/no question about permission keeps the modal in position two.

exercises.skill: Choosing the right modal for strength and relationship
exercises.english: Are you able to help me tomorrow?
exercises.german: Kannst du mir morgen helfen?
exercises.why: Ability is können; the accusative pronoun mir stays in the field.

exercises.skill: Choosing the right modal for strength and relationship
exercises.english: We are supposed to be there at nine.
exercises.german: Wir sollen um neun dort sein.
exercises.why: An arrangement reported by a third party takes sollen plus the verb sein.

exercises.skill: Choosing the right modal for strength and relationship
exercises.english: She wants to study medicine in Vienna.
exercises.german: Sie will in Wien Medizin studieren.
exercises.why: A stated plan is wollen and takes no ability or obligation modal after it.

exercises.skill: Choosing the right modal for strength and relationship
exercises.english: Nobody is allowed to smoke on the balcony.
exercises.german: Niemand darf auf dem Balkon rauchen.
exercises.why: A general prohibition is a negated dürfen, and niemand as subject keeps verb two.

exercises.skill: Choosing the right modal for strength and relationship
exercises.english: I would prefer to walk.
exercises.german: Ich würde lieber zu Fuß gehen.
exercises.why: The Konjunktiv II of mögen expresses a preference, and gehen stays in the Infinitiv.

exercises.skill: Choosing the right modal for strength and relationship
exercises.english: You have to take the stairs; the lift is broken.
exercises.german: Du musst die Treppe nehmen; der Aufzug ist kaputt.
exercises.why: A consequence takes a single müssen in the present, with a semicolon before the reason.

exercises.skill: Choosing the right modal for strength and relationship
exercises.english: You may not tell him that you have to do it.
exercises.german: Du darfst ihm nicht sagen, dass du das machen musst.
exercises.why: Two different levels in two clauses: prohibition in the main clause, obligation in the reported speech.

exercises.skill: Choosing the right modal for strength and relationship
exercises.english: You cannot afford something like that.
exercises.german: So etwas kannst du dir nicht leisten.
exercises.why: A negated können reports impossibility, and the modal needs no second level of its own.
